newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil telecom vote seen in early June or later.
newsitem.headline: Brazil telecom vote seen in early June or later.

text.p: The lower house of Brazil's Congress is not expected to vote on a bill regulating the country's telecommunications sector until early June or later, a congressional source said on Thursday.

The lower house, the Chamber of Deputies, must first approve a motion to grant urgent status to a measure containing the proposed General Telecommunications Law, allowing the bill to be placed on the agenda in early June, said a spokeswoman for Deputy Alberto Goldman, who drafted the legislation.
"We are waiting today for a request for urgent consideration so it can go in the first week of June," the spokeswoman said. "Without that, it will take a lot longer."

The law, which also would authorize the privatization of the federal Telebras system, was sent to the full chamber after approval Tuesday by a special panel of deputies on a 21-to-7 vote. If approved by the full chamber, the bill would be sent to the Senate for a final vote.

Brazil's Congress has decided to take next week off because attendance had been expected to be low. Also, there is lingering confusion over allegations that some deputies took bribes to vote in favor of a re-election bill earlier this year.

The spokeswoman said the committee made few changes in Goldman's original draft, even though there is disagreement over how much foreign participation to allow in the sector and how much autonomy to give a new telecoms regulator.

Analysts expect debate in the lower house to focus on the independence of the watchdog -- National Telecommunications Agency (Antel) -- as well as attempts by some deputies to set a limit on foreign investment.
The bill approved by the committee places no restriction on foreign participation, though it allows the executive branch to set limits on a case-by-case basis.
It also provides for a separate budget for Antel to help ensure its independence.
